I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is familiar to me, the well is reliable, and I know the weather patterns. My body isn't as strong as it was, and I'm alone now, so I keep things manageable. I split my 6 mu evenly — 3 mu wheat, 3 mu maize — same as always. No reason to change what has fed me this long.

**Wheat (winter, planted October):** I'll buy improved seed from the county supply station, same variety I've used the past few years — good resistance, decent yield. I rotary till after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I put down base fertilizer before sowing — diammonium phosphate and urea together — then topdress urea again at jointing. I irrigate four times: once before sowing to get good germination, the winter freeze water to protect roots, jointing stage, and heading. I spray herbicide in winter and then a combined fungicide-insecticide at heading for rust and aphids. That's two pesticide runs.

**Maize (summer, planted mid-June):** Right after wheat harvest I plant directly — no tilling, no time for it in June heat. I use hybrid seed, the kind they sell at the village store. Heavy nitrogen — I split it, some at planting, the rest at jointing. Three irrigations: one at emergence if it's dry, one at jointing, one at grain fill. Two pesticide applications — herbicide early, then something for corn borer if I see damage.

I don't experiment at my age. I do what I know.
